_meta.title: Drosophila melanogaster behavioral validation targets for a smell/taste foraging model
_meta.confidence_scale: VERIFIED = number read in fetched full text/abstract/supplement; SUMMARIZER = via a page summary; FIGURE-ONLY = value exists only in a figure (not given here); ESTIMATE = ours

knaden2012_valence.citation: Knaden M, Strutz A, Ahsan J, Sachse S, Hansson BS 2012 Cell Reports 1:392-399, doi:10.1016/j.celrep.2012.03.002

assay.type: two-trap choice assay (NOT T-maze): odor trap vs solvent trap, 24 h, 25 C, 70% RH
assay.flies: 50 flies/replicate, ~1:1 sex, 4-5 d old, starved 24 h
assay.AI_formula: AI = (O - C)/50, O/C = flies in odor/control trap; flies in neither trap reduce |AI|
assay.dilution: 2 uL odorant in 200 uL water + 0.2 uL Triton X-100 on filter paper (1:100) -- mu symbols garbled in PDF text; 1:100 is our reading (UNVERIFIED)
assay.stability: trap-entrance concentration decreased <10x over 24 h, little in first 4 h (Fig S1)

glomerular_valence.imaging: odors 1e-1 or 1e-3 in mineral oil, further 1:10 in air stream
glomerular_valence.caveat: DM5 attractive here conflicts with Semmelhack & Wang 2009 (DM5 reduces vinegar attraction); authors attribute to 24 h still-air trap vs acute olfactometer assay

caveats: single concentration for all odorants -> AIs are not dose-independent valences
starved flies, 24 h integration -> reflects trap entry, not plume tracking

other_valence_datasets.paper: Badel L, Ohta K, Tsuchimoto Y, Kazama H 2016 Neuron 90:994 doi:10.1016/j.neuron.2016.05.022
other_valence_datasets.finding: preference predicted by summing normalized glomerular (PN) responses; context can switch preference

other_valence_datasets.paper: Mohamed AAM et al. 2019 Nat Commun (PMC6416470)
other_valence_datasets.finding: ethyl acetate 1e-2 (attractive; DM1-DM4) vs benzaldehyde 1e-1 (aversive; DL1, DL5); benzaldehyde or geosmin in mixture suppress DM1-DM4 (lateral inhibition)
geosmin (Or56a/DA2) aversion overrides attraction to vinegar, oviposition and feeding

Semmelhack_Wang_2009.citation: Semmelhack JL & Wang JW 2009 Nature 459:218 doi:10.1038/nature07983 (PMC2702439)
Semmelhack_Wang_2009.assay: single fly, four-quadrant arena; PI = time in odor quadrant (-100..+100%); concentration by PID (ppm isobutylene equivalents)

Ko_2015_starved_vs_fed.assay: % single flies reaching source within 10 min
Ko_2015_starved_vs_fed.starved: 23 -> 60 from 0.5% to 25% vinegar, declining at higher concentrations

Root_2011.citation: Root CM, Ko KI, Jafari A, Wang JW 2011 Cell 145:133 (PMC3073827)
Root_2011.finding: 17-24 h starvation: vinegar responses up in DM1, DM4, DM2, down in VM2, VA3; max sensitivity within 4 h; food search assay 1% vinegar, 10 min window; latencies FIGURE-ONLY

Becher_2010_wind_tunnel.citation: Becher PG et al. 2010 J Chem Ecol 36:599 doi:10.1007/s10886-010-9794-2

Joseph_2009_oviposition_vs_position.citation: Joseph RM, Devineni AV, King IF, Heberlein U 2009 PNAS 106:11352 doi:10.1073/pnas.0901419106 (PMC2698888)
Joseph_2009_oviposition_vs_position.assay: 3 h, mated females; OI = (eggs AA - eggs control)/total; PI = position index

points.note: ~91% of eggs on AA food; pH ~3.5 food

Joseph_2009_oviposition_vs_position.feeding: no feeding preference for 5% AA (dye ingestion)
Joseph_2009_oviposition_vs_position.low_pH: below ~pH 2-3 AA food becomes aversive for oviposition too (Table S2, FIGURE-ONLY)
Joseph_2009_oviposition_vs_position.mechanism: egg-laying preference = taste; positional avoidance = olfaction

Ai_2010_smell.finding: T-maze (10 uL 10% AA) avoidance via Ir64a/DC4; Ir64a mutants residual avoidance index 20-25%; high-concentration cider vinegar (pH 2.5) avoided but same dilution neutralized to pH 7.5 attractive; 25% vinegar attractive while acetic acid of the same acidity is not

Devineni_2019_taste_hunger.fed: 1-10% AA PER ~ water; 10% AA reduces PER to 300 mM sucrose 79% -> 44%
Devineni_2019_taste_hunger.starved_2d: 86% PER to 10% AA; AA no longer suppresses sugar PER (5-300 mM) and enhances PER to 5-10 mM sucrose; 7/10 starved flies ingested 5% AA via legs

Rimal_2019_two_choice_taste.citation: Rimal S et al. 2019 Cell Rep doi:10.1016/j.celrep.2019.01.042

Chen_Amrein_2017_oviposition.citation: Chen Y & Amrein H 2017 Curr Biol 27:2741
Chen_Amrein_2017_oviposition.substrate: 100 mM sucrose agar + acetic acid 10/100/500 mM (or citric/tartaric 1-100 mM)
Chen_Amrein_2017_oviposition.finding: tarsal Ir25a/Ir76b sour GRNs drive oviposition preference; OI FIGURE-ONLY

Ogueta_2010.citation: Ogueta M, Cibik O, Eltrop R, Schneider A, Scholz H 2010 Chem Senses 35:813
Ogueta_2010.finding: prefer food with up to 5% ethanol over no ethanol; avoid 23% ethanol

Schneider_2012.citation: Schneider A et al. 2012 PLoS One 7:e52007 (PMC3527413)

Azanchi_2013_oviposition.citation: Azanchi R, Kaun KR, Heberlein U 2013 PNAS 110:21153 (PMC3876210)
Azanchi_2013_oviposition.findings: preference significant from 3% (P=0.04); 5% preferred over 1, 3 and 10%; 5% vs 7.5% n.s.; 3% > 1%; total eggs reduced when choice includes 7.5 or 10%; cites rotting fruit <=5% ethanol

van_Breugel_2018.finding: ethanol attractive in all activity states; flies spend ~2x longer searching near ethanol than CO2 or vinegar; ethanol + CO2 approached most

model_curve_ESTIMATE.unit: relative attraction (1 = max); combines Ogueta 2010, Azanchi 2013, Devineni 2009 (15% attractive in traps). ESTIMATE

Suh_2004.citation: Suh GS et al. 2004 Nature 431:854 doi:10.1038/nature02980
Suh_2004.finding: avoidance at levels as low as 0.1% via V glomerulus

Faucher_2006.finding: avoid +0.1-1% above ambient; no response to +0.02%; +0.02% CO2 does not reduce vinegar attraction (except against vinegar background in females)

Faucher_2013.citation: Faucher CP, Hilker M, de Bruyne M 2013 PLoS One 8:e56361

Braecker_2013.finding: strong avoidance >0.02% above atmospheric; starved flies partly suppress avoidance in presence of vinegar (fed flies do not); starved-state avoidance needs MB and biVPN; indices FIGURE-ONLY

Ai_2010.finding: Gr21a/Gr63a-silenced flies still avoid CO2 above ~5% via DC4 (carbonic acid)

Wasserman_2013.citation: Wasserman S, Salomon A, Frye MA 2013 Curr Biol 23:301 (PMC3810385)
Wasserman_2013.finding: tethered flying flies track a narrow plume from 100% CO2 source (plume ~+/-45 deg at half max; delivered concentration not stated); requires Orco and octopamine, not Gr21a/Gr63a

van_Breugel_2018.findings: walking flies avoid 5% CO2 after 10 min acclimation but attracted after 2 h; attraction only in active/high-speed state (dusk, starved); starved slow (~1.5 mm/s) flies averse to 5% CO2 but attracted to ethanol; attraction requires Ir25a (not Gr63a, Ir64a); 5% most effective of 1.7/5/15%; 2-day apple-juice ferment preferred over 7-12-day ferments (indices FIGURE-ONLY); wind 40 cm/s

Ucpunar_Grunwald_Kadow_2021.finding: 30 h food-deprived flies avoid ambient air (~400 ppm) in favor of CO2-free air; Gr63a mutants no preference 1% vs ambient

CO2.banana_context: yellow banana emits ~200 uL CO2/min (~+0.1% in 145 mL/min flow), black banana ~30 uL/min (Faucher 2006) -> near the avoidance threshold for resting flies in enclosed space; fermenting fruit emits more (chemistry.json)

starvation_shift_summary.vinegar: starved > fed at all concentrations (Ko 2015); DM1/DM2/DM4 up, VM2/VA3 down (Root 2011); DM5 threshold 4x higher (Ko 2015) -> high-concentration aversion weakened; wind tunnel 62% vs <20% (Becher 2010)
starvation_shift_summary.CO2: hunger + food odor suppress CO2 avoidance (Braecker 2013, Lewis 2015); activity/flight flips CO2 to attractive (van Breugel 2018)
starvation_shift_summary.acetic_acid_taste: aversive in fed -> appetitive in 1-2 d starved (Devineni 2019)
starvation_shift_summary.sugar_bitter_taste: sugar sensitivity x4.6, bitter sensitivity /4.8 at 2 d starvation (Inagaki 2014)

ethanol_food.citation: Devineni AV & Heberlein U 2009 Curr Biol 19:2126 (PMC2805771)
ethanol_food.assay: CAFE, 15% ethanol in 5% sucrose + 5% yeast extract vs same without ethanol
ethanol_food.finding: preference positive day 1, increases, stable by days 4-5; dose dependence 5-25% emerges days 4-5; PER: 0.1-40% ethanol no PER, dose-dependently reduces sucrose PER; internal ethanol ~5.2 mM (continuous), 26-45 mM after starve-refeed

ethanol_food.citation: Pohl JB et al. 2012 Alcohol Clin Exp Res 36:1903 (PMC3414655)
ethanol_food.finding: no preference at 1% ethanol; preference at 5, 10, 15%; vs calorie-matched alternative usually no preference for 10% (can reverse); internal ethanol <=4 mM (3.08 mM measured)

yeast_vs_sucrose.citation: Vargas MA et al. 2010 Curr Biol 20:1006 (PMC2885474)
yeast_vs_sucrose.assay: radiolabel choice 4% yeast extract vs 5% sucrose
yeast_vs_sucrose.finding: mated females eat significantly more yeast than virgins; females more than males

yeast_vs_sucrose.citation: Ribeiro C & Dickson BJ 2010 Curr Biol 20:1000
yeast_vs_sucrose.finding: protein-deprived flies prefer yeast; mating increases yeast preference via SPR in ppk+ neurons, neuronal TOR/S6K

yeast_vs_sucrose.citation: Corrales-Carvajal VM, Faisal AA, Ribeiro C 2016 eLife 5:e19920 (PMC5108593)
yeast_vs_sucrose.assay: 180 g/L yeast and 180 g/L sucrose patches (flyPAD/video); 3 d pre-feeding on holidic diets (AA-rich, suboptimal, AA-free)

findings.virgin_females: more total feeding time on sucrose than yeast
findings.mated_females: more on yeast; mating adds long (>=20 s) yeast bouts

yeast_vs_sucrose.citation: Walker SJ, Corrales-Carvajal VM, Ribeiro C 2015 Curr Biol 25:2621
yeast_vs_sucrose.finding: mating induces sex-peptide-dependent sodium appetite (independent of need; SAG neuron silencing)

yeast_vs_sucrose.citation: Toshima N & Tanimura T 2012 J Exp Biol 215:2827
yeast_vs_sucrose.finding: flies raised without amino acids strongly prefer 10 mM amino-acid solution; CAFE intake >7x controls (females), ~3x (males) at 6 h

sugar.citation: Dus M, Min S, Keene AC, Lee GY, Suh GSB 2011 PNAS 108:11819 (PMC3136275)
sugar.finding: 100 mM sucrose vs plain agar; sugar-blind Gr5a;Gr64a mutants do not eat after 5 h starvation but prefer sucrose after 22 h; prefer metabolizable over non-metabolizable sugars (post-ingestive sensing)

sugar.PER_dose_response: see receptors.json gustatory.PER_behavior_sucrose (Inagaki 2014: 50-60% PER at 800 mM fed, 300 mM 1 d, 200 mM 2 d starved)

sugar.gap: clean two-choice sucrose concentration-preference curve (e.g. Tanimura 1982) not obtained

contact_feeding_preferences.acetic_acid_food: see concentration_dependence.acetic_acid (Joseph 2009 no feeding preference at 5%; Devineni 2019 hunger switch; Rimal 2019 two-choice curve)

polyamines.citation: Hussain A et al. 2016 PLoS Biol 14:e1002455
polyamines.finding: mated females prefer 1 mM putrescine/cadaverine; virgins only lowest levels

flight_plume_tracking.citation: van Breugel F & Dickinson MH 2014 Curr Biol 24:274 doi:10.1016/j.cub.2013.12.023

walking_complex_plume.heading_vs_encounter_rate: 88.6 deg from upwind at 0 Hz, slope -21.6 deg/Hz; bias decays to ~4.5 deg/Hz within 5 s w/o encounters; encounter frequency filtered tau = 2 s

dispersal.citation: Leitch KJ, Ponce FV, Dickson WB, van Breugel F, Dickinson MH 2021 PNAS 118:e2013342118 (PMC8092610)

budick_dickinson_2006.finding: hungry flies fly upwind by default; plume contact reduces crosswind and speeds upwind flight; plume loss triggers casting

navigation_anchors.odor_detection_distance: GAP: no direct measurement. Derive from plume dilution + ORN thresholds (receptors.json) and source strength (chemistry.json).

suggested_validation_tests_ESTIMATE: Ripe vs rotting (yeast-colonized) banana two-choice: expect rotting preferred by starved flies (Becher 2012 yeast > fruit; ethanol+acetic+2-phenylethanol synergy Zhu 2003, Becher 2010).
Vinegar-like dose sweep: attraction rising 0.5-12 ppm, falling at >=32 ppm via DM5 (Semmelhack 2009); hunger removes much of the drop (Ko 2015).
Silencing ORN_DM1 should abolish low-concentration vinegar/ethyl acetate attraction (Semmelhack 2009).
Ethanol oviposition/odor preference peaking ~5% (Azanchi 2013; Ogueta 2010), aversive by ~23%.
Resting fly near fruit with CO2 +0.1-1% should show avoidance, suppressed by food odor when starved (Faucher 2006; Braecker 2013).
Mated protein-deprived female should shift contact feeding to yeast (1.6x feeding, ~3x shorter latency; Corrales-Carvajal 2016).
Starved fly should accept 1-10% acetic acid on proboscis (86% PER at 10%) whereas fed fly rejects (Devineni 2019).
biggest_gaps: Knaden AIs are single-concentration trap indices; no acetoin, geosmin or CO2 in the panel
Many fed/starved and virgin/mated magnitudes are figure-only (Root 2011, Braecker 2013, Lewis 2015, Ribeiro & Dickson 2010, Walker 2015, Badel 2016)
Knaden odor dilution (1:100) inferred from garbled PDF
No measured odor detection distance for banana/ferment sources
